outputs.summary: createGitRepo (src/test/gitRepo.ts) now retries temp-folder creation plus `git init` as one unit. It makes up to 3 attempts with a 50 ms then 100 ms backoff, and each attempt uses a fresh temp folder; a failed attempt's folder is removed with removeScratch. The retry fires only on the busy/locked-folder class that the ticket names: errno EBUSY/EPERM/EACCES from the temp-folder calls (syscall mkdtemp/mkdir/realpath), or git stderr matching `could not lock`, `Device or resource busy` or `Permission denied` from `git init`. Every other failure throws its original error on the first attempt: a different git error, the same errno from spawnSync git (git cannot start or is missing), ENOSPC, or EBUSY on a non-temp syscall. Any failure after `git init` also throws at once, including in the initial commit and later repo.git()/commit() calls. Each retry writes a console.warn line containing git's stderr, so a retry cannot hide a flake. execFileSync, createTempRepo, warn and pause can be injected through an optional `createGitRepo(overrides)`; the existing zero-argument callers are unchanged. Red team: I reviewed my own diff, and a security-reviewer subagent tried to refute it. It found no transport bypass, token leak, deletion of a pre-existing folder, or renderer control of the parent. Fixed: (1, medium) a second clone into the same parent waited unseen in the runner's per-folder queue, so its cancel did nothing; now one clone runs at a time per parent and the second is refused with a message. (2) A cancel during cleanup reported true; now nothing is left to stop once git has ended. Cancelling a finished clone into an untracked parent now answers { cancelled: false }, not unauthorized. (3) EACCES/EPERM/EROFS/ENAMETOOLONG on the target are now invalid_input with the reason, not 'Git failed unexpectedly'. (4) The .git name check strips the code points HFS+ ignores. (5) ssh hosts and users must be plain names after %-decoding (closes '[-o…]', '%2F-o…', '$(…)' users; git also blocked these). (8) Each repository-list limit, the account-switch branch and the runner onExit test are now non-vacuous. Rejected, with reasons: (6) networkAuth reads core.sshCommand with cwd = the clone parent, so a repository around the parent can turn BatchMode off. git still runs without a TTY in its own session, so it cannot hang on a prompt, and networkAuth is shared with sync and branches. (7) An account switch mid-listing returns that answer uncached; the renderer re-lists on account change. onExit fires on the runner's own notion of gone ('error' or 'close'), the same one its write queue uses, and the 10 s bound covers the rest. followUps.body: credentialArgs passes the token as DM_GITHUB_TOKEN in git's env, so every process git starts inherits it. A per-run trampoline (a one-time secret handed to an askpass/credential helper that asks main over a local socket, as GitHub Desktop does) would keep it out of child environments. Medium; security.
followUps.title: Keep the GitHub token out of the environment of git hooks and helpers

followUps.body: Pull runs `git pull --no-rebase --no-edit`; with pull.ff=only a diverged branch fails instead of merging. Passing --ff honours 'pull merges' but overrides the person's setting. Product decision.
followUps.title: Decide how pull treats a user's pull.ff=only
